ov: A medium-sized spotted wild cat of the Americas and the largest member of its genus. It climbs, leaps and swims well, hunts mostly at night and prefers dense cover near water. Each ocelot has its own unique coat pattern.

why.ac: Active mainly at twilight and at night.

rg: From the southwestern United States (Texas and Arizona) through Mexico and Central America to northern Argentina.
df: Small mammals such as rodents, rabbits, armadillos and opossums, plus fish, crabs, insects, reptiles and birds.
fx: It usually hunts animals weighing less than 1 kg.
Its name comes from the Nahuatl (Aztec) word ōcēlōtl.
